title: Black Hole Thermodynamics
description: A black hole has a temperature, so it has an entropy, and that entropy is its horizon's area in Planck units, divided by four. The most information any region can hold is set by its surface, not its volume.

puzzle.goal: A horizon of area A carries an entropy S, counted in units of Boltzmann's constant, set only by c, G and ħ. Write S.
puzzle.name: Bekenstein-Hawking entropy
puzzle.ask: Find S in units of 10⁷⁰ k (u = @{u}) for a solar-mass hole, A = @{A} m² (c = 2.998e8, G = 6.674e-11, h = 1.0546e-34 for ħ).
puzzle.method: Integrate dS = dE/T with E = Mc² and the Hawking temperature: S grows as M², which is the area.
